H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller has four flat gait phases: Early Stance, Middle Stance, Late Stance, and Swing; no parent state or nested sub-FSM is described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Switching uses ankle angle and derivative: heel strike uses onset of plantarflexion plus theta < Theta1; other transitions use dorsiflexion onset, theta > Theta2, and theta < Theta3.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Each state selects impedance parameters, generates desired ankle torque, converts it to desired actuator force, and drives a PID-controlled pneumatic valve.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper mentions unreliable foot switches as motivation for angle-based sensing, but gives no fault state, recovery transition, or global safe escape.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and gait-event definitions are in Section 3.1, per-phase impedance behavior in Section 3.2, switching guards in Section 3.3, and tuned parameters in Table 2.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Biomechanical terms such as heel strike, foot flat, toe off, and swing are defined or operationalized in the paper rather than left as unstated transition rules.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: State actions are described narratively as spring-like impedance behavior per phase, requiring attribution back to the FSM states.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: At least heel strike combines ankle angular-velocity direction with the additional comparison theta < Theta1.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state or superstate with its own entry, during, or exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault, emergency, abort, or safe-state rule is specified.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The guard set includes one meaningful compound angle-plus-velocity condition and several threshold comparisons, but not three or more arithmetic/boolean compound guards.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No cross-cutting transition over multiple substates and no parent-level continuous monitor is present.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete control commands: desired torque, desired actuator force, and pneumatic valve command.

key_nl_quotes: For the implementation of the controller, a finite-state machine is constructed and executed in real-time.
The state machine ... generates the desired actuation torque command for the powered ankle joint.
one_line_pitch: A flat but action-heavy gait-phase EFSM whose angle/velocity guards and continuous impedance-to-force-to-valve actions stress guard and action recovery.
rationale: This is a clear state-machine sample with strong guarded switching and non-trivial per-state control actions, both directly tied to weak baseline dimensions. Its baseline-trap density is high because state definitions, impedance actions, guards, and parameter values are split across multiple paper sections. It is secondary rather than top-tier because it has no hierarchy, no fault recovery, no parallelism, and only a narrow pyfcstm-specific advantage.
